findings: GetYourGuide search is not deterministic. The same query, same parameters, minutes apart, returns a different three. 'Warner Bros Studio Tour London' came back all-Studio-Tour four runs in five and Tower of London plus Madame Tussauds on the fifth. No data-gyg-q value can be trusted to show the right products every page view - use data-gyg-tour-ids for anything the article's argument depends on, and keep a query slot only where a stray Tower of London ticket would do no harm.

Any query missing the words 'Warner Bros' AND 'London' can fall back to the viewer's own location. From here that meant New York products priced in euros. A reader in London would presumably get London junk instead, but it would still be junk.

Adding &location_id=57 to the frame URL fixed the dead 'Harry Potter Studio Tour' query and returned London results. Whether the embed script exposes a matching data attribute is untested - worth checking before relying on it.

There is no entrance-only ticket on GetYourGuide, and that is by design: the operator's Travel Partners page requires approved distributors to sell tickets as part of a package. Everything GetYourGuide lists bundles transport, a cruise or a guide, so nothing on the platform is a bare markup on the GBP 58.50 door price.

What GetYourGuide sells that the operator does not: a return coach from Victoria (31392, GBP 85) or King's Cross (82665, GBP 97), a return train package from Euston (679208, GBP 75), Zone 1 hotel pickup in a small executive vehicle (297085, GBP 155), a fully guided visit (63735, GBP 100), a private vehicle (596540, GBP 120), and combinations with Oxford (61450) or a Thames cruise (469400, 408850).

The free electric shuttle from Watford Junction is already included in the door price. Two listings (469400, 679208) name it as an inclusion, which is accurate but adds nothing on its own - do not let it read as a reason to pay more.

No reseller was found charging far above the door price for entry alone. The nearest thing to a bad-value listing is 408850 at GBP 85 next to 469400 at GBP 59 for what reads as the same Studio Tour plus Thames cruise bundle.
avoid: 596540 (GBP 120) and 652990 (GBP 108) are private transfers with NO entry ticket - their own listings say tickets must be bought separately from the official site. Never present either as a way to book the Studio Tour.
Do not quote 469400's GBP 59 without checking what that option actually buys: it is 50p above the door price for a ticket plus a Thames cruise, and a same-named bundle (408850) sells at GBP 85.
Do not repeat 31392's highlights line about wandering 'the pretty streets of royal Windsor' - it is copy from a different tour and the itinerary does not go to Windsor.

Broad or location-free queries return, variously: NYC Broadway shows and helicopter tours in euros, Venice and Nevsehir airport transfers, Warner Bros. Studio Tour Hollywood (55864), Warner Park Madrid (400697), Warner Bros. Studio Tour Tokyo (975381), Tower of London, Madame Tussauds, The Shard, West End musicals and a junior inflatable park ticket.
63735's transport arrangements are unverified - its page would not render. Do not write that the guided tour includes or excludes a transfer until someone has opened it.
